project_scope.note: Penstemon cobaea is the best current family visual reference; the website's canonical Plantaginaceae species set remains sparse.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: For Penstemon-style plants, inspect inside the fused bilateral corolla: four fertile stamens plus a sterile fifth stamen/staminode.
family_diagnostics.habit: Mostly herbs; leaves simple and without stipules.
family_diagnostics.flower: Fused usually zygomorphic corolla; commonly 2 or 4 fertile stamens, with staminodes in some lineages.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Penstemon: four fertile stamens and a fifth staminode, but NOT family-universal. Plantago: dense small-flowered spike and pyxis (lid-opening capsule); Veronica: often two stamens. Check fruit and genus before calling the family.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Penstemon gives you a memorable doorway into Plantaginaceae: four fertile stamens plus one sterile beardtongue inside a bilateral tube.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the Penstemon gestalt
steps.look_for: Herbaceous habit with opposite simple leaves and large bilateral tubular flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: A strong local Plantaginaceae teaching form.

steps.title: 2 · Find the beardtongue
steps.look_for: Four fertile stamens plus a sterile fifth stamen/staminode.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the signature Penstemon mechanism behind the common name beardtongue.

steps.title: 3 · Follow to the capsule
steps.look_for: A dry capsule with many seeds rather than mint-family nutlets.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit separates Plantaginaceae from Lamiaceae in many local tubular-flowered herbs.

steps.title: 4 · Remember family breadth
steps.look_for: The family includes forms that do not look like Penstemon at all.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents the learner from turning a genus-level staminode into a family-wide rule.

comparisons.title: Plantaginaceae vs Lamiaceae
comparisons.rule: Plantaginaceae commonly has a many-seeded capsule; Lamiaceae commonly matures four nutlets or a drupaceous fruit.

comparisons.title: Plantaginaceae vs Acanthaceae
comparisons.rule: Acanthaceae commonly has a capsule with retinacula/jaculators that launch seeds; Plantaginaceae lacks that mechanism.

visual_lesson.caveat: The current visual lesson is intentionally Penstemon-centered; family breadth should expand as more local genera are promoted.

reconciliation_2026_10_14.look_here_first: LOOK FIRST by genus: Penstemon has 4 fertile stamens plus a fifth sterile staminode in a bilateral tube. Plantago has tiny spike flowers and a circumscissile capsule (pyxis); Veronica often has 2 stamens and a 4-lobed corolla. Broad Plantaginaceae is NOT uniformly bilabiate or staminode-bearing. Confirm fruit and current genus.
reconciliation_2026_10_14.local_confusion: Confusable Lamiales: Acanthaceae may have seed-support retinacula in a 2-locular capsule (not universal); Plantaginaceae capsules lack those hooks. Lamiaceae typically makes four nutlets, often with a gynobasic style. Orobanchaceae includes green hemiparasites; Scrophulariaceae older broad placements differ from current taxonomy. Corolla color is weak.
reconciliation_2026_10_14.photo_handoff: Photo locks: Penstemon dissected 4 anthers + staminode; Plantago flower/pyxis lid and seeds; Veronica 2 stamens and unequal corolla lobes; Bacopa/Mecardonia flower-to-fruit; matched Plantaginaceae capsule vs Ruellia retinacula and mint nutlets. Route remaining Leucospora, Maurandella, Nuttallanthus with genus-specific floral photos.

penstemon_visual_extension.title: Beardtongue flower parts
penstemon_visual_extension.look_here_first: On a flower throat close-up, distinguish four fertile stamens from the often hairy fifth sterile stamen, called the staminode. Inspect the calyx, upper leaf attachment, and dry seed capsule.
